T. Purushotham Rao vs The Union Of India And 9 Others on 8
June, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Mummineni Sudheer Kumar
 Writ Petition No.32008 of 2022
Order:

sentences.text:
Heard Sri Avinash Desai, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner and Sri Gadi Praveen Kumar,
learned Deputy Solicitor General of India for respondent Nos.1 to 6.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that his grandfather was the absolute owner and possessor of the land admeasuring Ac.0.27 gts., equivalent to 3267 Sq. Yds. situated in Sy.No.602/A (602/1)
corresponding to GLR No.259 in Alwal Village and Mandal, Medchal-Malkajgiri District and the said land has been in possession and enjoyment of the family of the petitioner for the past more than 90 years and the same is claimed to have been succeeded by the petitioner.
It is the further case of the petitioner that the name of the grandfather of the petitioner i.e., Mr. T.Kishan Rao was recorded as owner and possessor of the subject land in the Revenue records.
3. The petitioner also placed reliance on the copies of the various Pahanies that are filed along with the Writ Petition.

However, respondent No.4 is alleged to have taken possession over the subject land without following any due process of law and without paying any compensation under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act, 2013'), in illegal and high- handed manner

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: and has been continuing in possession of the subject land.

Having been aggrieved by the said circumstances, the petitioner claimed to have submitted a representation, dated 12.10.2021, to respondent No.6, who is the custodian of the Defence Estate and marking a copy of the same to several other authorities,
including the Revenue officials of the State requesting to pay monetary compensation or to allot equivalent land in the Secunderabad Contonment Limits.

4. It is the further case of the petitioner that respondent No.6, after having considered the claim of the petitioner, addressed a letter No.T&AP/1101/ACQ/I/8, dated 22.03.2022, seeking certain clarifications and certified copies of the documents from the petitioner.
The petitioner claimed to have submitted a detailed reply in response to the said letter, dated 22.03.2022, by furnishing all the clarifications that are sought by respondent No.6 on 30.03.2022.
However, no further communication is received from respondent No.6.
Therefore, the petitioner claimed to have addressed a reminder, dated 17.05.2022, to respondent No.6.

Having failed to get any response from respondent No.6, the petitioner approached this Court complaining inaction on the part of the respondents in considering the representation submitted by the petitioner.
5. This matter earlier came up on 10.08.2022 and again on 13.09.2022 and though time was sought for filing counters, no counter affidavits are filed by the respondents as on date.

sentences.text:
Sri Avinash Desai, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner, submitted that the respondents failed to file their counter affidavit even after lapse of more than six months and any further delay in disposal of the matter would cause prejudice to the petitioner as they were already dispossessed from their land long back and sought indulgence of this Court to consider the Writ Petition for disposal by directing respondent No.6 to consider the representation, dated 12.10.2021,
together with the clarifications furnished by the petitioner through his letter, dated 30.03.2022, and pass appropriate orders thereon within a time to be specified by this Court.
7. Sri Gadi Praveen Kumar, learned Deputy Solicitor General of India, expressed his no objection for disposal of the Writ Petition in the lines as requested by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

8. In the light of the above, the Writ Petition is disposed of directing respondent No.6 to consider the representation, dated 12.10.2021, read with clarificatory letter, dated 30.03.2022, submitted by the petitioner and pass appropriate orders thereon, in accordance with law, within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition, shall stand closed.
No costs.

____________________________________ MUMMINENI SUDHEER KUMAR, J Date:
